summary.headline: Narayana Hrudayalaya Q2 FY27: India IP volumes up ~4% YoY, ARPOB up to INR19.5mn annualised, and insurance plus clinic losses cut to ~INR22 crore from ~INR33 crore QoQ.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as a strong quarter for India, with IP volumes up about 4% YoY, OP footfall up about 12.5%, and annualised ARPOB up from INR17.5 million to INR19.5 million. Operating margin in India was stated at more than 26%, helped by operating leverage on largely fixed clinical and nursing costs, which fell about 1.9% QoQ. Combined insurance and clinic losses narrowed to about INR22 crore from about INR33 crore last quarter. The UK business showed a revenue dip QoQ and no margin benefit yet from cost synergies, while Cayman insurance losses fell to $1.1 million from $3.7 million.

financial_highlights.change: management described as among best in industry
from $3.7 million prior quarter and $5.4 million two quarters ago

financial_highlights.metric: International patients share of India hospital revenue

segments.name: India hospitals
segments.commentary: IP volumes up ~4% YoY and OP footfall up ~12.5%; ARPOB rose to INR19.5 million annualised, with margin above 26%. Occupancy stable at 60% to 65%, and no bed additions made so far.

segments.name: India insurance
segments.commentary: Loss narrowed to ~INR14 crore from ~INR19 crore QoQ. Management said it is building a retail direct book and SME book, and will not pursue growth until losses are reduced.

segments.name: India clinics
segments.commentary: Loss reduced to ~INR8 crore from ~INR14 crore QoQ. Clinics will be merged into the hospital segment from the next reporting period, so only insurance will be reported separately.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped QoQ due to NHS contracting slowdown and slow private-channel build-out. Cost synergies (consumables, supply chain, GCC, software) are running ahead of plan but are not yet flowing to earnings. Management cited net debt of about INR1,700 crore and EBITDA margin decline from ~8.8% to ~7% (analyst figures, not confirmed by management).

segments.name: Cayman
segments.commentary: Hospital business described as performing well, with growth now expected to slow as the island market is a constraint. Insurance losses cut to $1.1 million from $3.7 million, with a repricing reset in January 2027 for a smaller cohort and the major reset in July 2027.

guidance_outlook: India IP footfall expected to pick up from Eastern cluster in Q3 after a government-scheme porting issue in Bengal settles; management expects good IP and OP growth in Q3 and Q4.
Management does not target margins and does not guide on them; Q2 is seasonally strong and Q3 is expected to be slightly muted.
Cayman insurance: management expects losses to be negligible before July 2027 and to have exited most unprofitable books from July 2027.
Group ROCE at 15% to 16%, with the UK dilution of about 4% to 5% to be bridged over about 5 years; UK time horizon of 5 to 7 years.
ALOS to move toward 4.0 to 4.1 days over the next 4 to 6 quarters (currently 4.3 to 4.5 days).
Bed additions of about 635 are planned in FY28; management will give commissioning guidance one quarter in advance.
capex_capacity: No bed additions made in the recent quarters; occupancy at 60% to 65% on midnight-bed basis, not a managed metric.
About 635 beds to be added in FY28 per analyst question; management confirmed commissioning timelines will be given one quarter in advance.
Group ROCE currently low as the company is in the capex phase after Cayman and UK investments and India expansion.
UK digital platform (Athma) expected to be certified in about 4 to 5 months, with implementation to follow.
GCC for international operations set up in Bangalore and rolled out for patient-facing communication recently.
demand_pricing: India ARPOB rose to INR19.5 million annualised from INR17.5 million YoY, driven by high-end procedures and robotics; management cites moderate price increases and balanced pricing.
Oncology price caps to go live from 9 November 2026; oncology is about 15% of India hospital revenue, and the capped drugs are only part of it.
Insurance payer collections slowed in India and Cayman in H1, while government payer collections in Q2 were slower than typical.
UK revenue fell QoQ as NHS contracting was slow and private-channel conversion is still in early stages; NHS contracts reset each year from 1 April.
Cayman international patients come mainly from other Caribbean islands; management says Cayman's best growth days are behind due to size constraints.
International patients in India are organic, mainly from Bangladesh, and are not specifically targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for further India margin improvement given ARPOB gap with peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not target margins; the focus is on volume growth and access. The margin reflects efficiency gains over 10 years in digitization, process and supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: How will the oncology price cap affect Narayana?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said oncology is about 15% of India hospital revenue and the capped drugs are only part of it; caps go live 9 November, and the company will support transparent pricing.

qa_highlights.question: When will insurance losses/combined ratio improve and will the company give up on insurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will neither give up nor pursue at any cost; no breakeven timeline given. Combined losses cut to ~INR22 crore from ~INR33 crore QoQ, with claims ratio trending down.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India IP footfall flat at about 60,000 for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Eastern cluster had a porting issue for certain government scheme patients in Bengal, expected to settle in Q3. Smaller Karnataka units are rationalising payer mix. IP footfall rose 6% QoQ and ~4% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is UK going as planned and what is the path to revenue recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost synergies are ahead of plan, but revenue has dipped due to NHS slowdown and slow private channel build-out. Management hopes revenue trajectory recovers but gave no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cayman insurance losses break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses fell from $5.4 million two quarters ago to $3.7 million and $1.1 million; the $1.1 million includes summer seasonality. Big repricing reset is in July 2027, with almost all unprofitable books exited from July onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash conversion fall to ~88% in H1 versus ~93% historically?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said UK conversion is not a problem (NHS pays on time and partly in advance); slower collections in India and Cayman, including insurance payers, explain the gap, expected to normalise over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove doctor and nurse cost decline to ~26% and is this structural?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said it reflects operating leverage on largely fixed clinical and nursing costs with revenue up ~9% QoQ. CFO said Q3 is typically muted, so investors should follow industry seasonality and not extrapolate Q2.

risks_watch: Insurance losses remain significant; combined ratio cited by an analyst at about 280% (not disputed by management), and there is no breakeven date.
UK revenue dip QoQ and reliance on NHS contracting, with private-channel conversion still early; cost synergies not yet visible in earnings.
Cash conversion in H1 about 88% vs ~93% historical, driven by slower collections in India and Cayman.
Oncology price cap effective 9 November 2026; impact still unclear.
Cybersecurity risk on interconnected IT systems; management said it is investing further in systems.
Eastern cluster IP footfall recovery in Q3 depends on settlement of government scheme porting issue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India operations and cost discipline, with management stating margins are a result of efficiency and not a target. More cautious and evasive on UK revenue recovery and on insurance breakeven, where no timelines were committed beyond the July 2027 Cayman repricing reset.
key_quotes: So margin expansion isn't the thing that we target. What we're looking for is accessing the largest pool of patients in all the cities that we operate in.
The clinic model is proven successful and merged into the numbers we'll report out for the hospital going forward.
We are not focusing on growth in insurance until we bring the losses down.
Typically, on a full-year basis, this normalizes: in some quarters collections are a little slow, but we catch up over the next few months.

adds.what: Approximately 635 beds planned for FY28 (analyst-cited; management to give commissioning guidance one quarter ahead)

growth.why: Management guided to good IP and OP growth in Q3 and Q4 (Eastern cluster recovery after Bengal porting issue) and ALOS toward 4.0-4.1 days, backed by ARPOB rising to INR19.5mn annualised and IP volumes up ~4% YoY, but gave no numeric revenue growth guidance and no bed additions until FY28 (~635 beds, analyst-cited).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India hospital margin is above 26% and doctor/nursing cost fell to ~26% of revenue on ~9% QoQ revenue growth, but management does not target margins and says Q3 will be slightly muted; insurance and clinic losses fell to ~INR22 crore from ~INR33 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 635 beds are planned for FY28 per an analyst citing the call, with management committing to give commissioning guidance one quarter ahead; no beds were added in recent quarters, and occupancy is 60-65%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IP volumes grew ~4% YoY and IP footfall ~6% QoQ, with OP footfall up ~12.5%; management expects good IP and OP growth in Q3 and Q4 as the Eastern cluster porting issue settles, though the brief gives no numeric volume guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Occupancy is 60-65% and no new beds have been added, so spare capacity exists; the FY28 bed plan is analyst-cited and management has not formally announced new capex, and the group is already in a capex phase after Cayman and UK investments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance and said Q3 is expected to be slightly muted, while oncology price caps go live 9 November 2026 with unclear impact on the ~15% oncology share of India hospital revenue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 is guided slightly muted, the oncology price cap starts 9 November 2026, UK revenue fell QoQ, and cash conversion dropped to ~88% in H1 from ~93% historically, though management did not formally cut guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The UK digital platform (Athma) is expected to be certified in about 4-5 months with implementation to follow, but no commercial launch date or revenue impact was given.

rows.label: ALOS reduction toward 4.0-4.1 days
rows.why: ALOS is guided down from the current 4.3-4.5 days toward 4.0-4.1 days, which would lift bed productivity without new beds.

rows.label: Insurance and Cayman loss reduction
rows.why: Combined insurance and clinic losses fell to ~INR22 crore from ~INR33 crore, and Cayman insurance losses fell to $1.1 million from $3.7 million, with the major Cayman repricing reset in July 2027; no India insurance breakeven date was given.

rows.label: Oncology price cap impact
rows.why: Oncology is about 15% of India hospital revenue and the caps go live 9 November 2026, but the impact is unclear because capped drugs are only part of that revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on India volumes, ARPOB and cost discipline, but cautious and evasive on UK revenue recovery, insurance breakeven and the oncology price cap; analysts pressed on insurance combined ratio (~280% cited), the UK dip and cash conversion.
